final_answer: This is my analysis. When an mRNA vaccine is injected into the body, the mRNA enters the cells of the body. The mRNA contains instructions for the cells to produce a protein that is found on the surface of the virus that the vaccine is designed to protect against. Once the cells have produced the protein, it is displayed on the surface of the cells. The immune system recognizes this protein as foreign and mounts an immune response. This immune response includes the production of antibodies and the activation of T cells. These immune cells remember the protein and are able to quickly respond if the person is exposed to the virus in the future. This is how mRNA vaccines work to protect against viral infections.
